question: Why do newborn babies need a vitamin K injection right after birth?

options.A: Breast milk contains zero traces of fat-soluble vitamins
options.B: Their liver is too large to process normal dietary proteins
options.C: Their sterile gut cannot yet synthesize the vitamin for blood clotting
options.D: They lose all stored maternal clotting factors during delivery

explanation: A newborn's tummy is completely sterile at first, meaning they don't have the gut bacteria needed to make vitamin K yet. The shot protects them from bleeding until their gut matures.

question: How can healthcare providers help patients who struggle with technology when using wearables?

options.A: By refusing care to anyone who does not understand technology immediately
options.B: By removing all digital screens from the monitoring equipment
options.C: By forcing all patients to buy the most expensive smartphone available
options.D: By providing simple, guided education and easy-to-use device interfaces

explanation: Patience and clear, step-by-step teaching help bridge the digital gap so every patient feels comfortable using their tracker.

question: Why is pre-contraception counseling so important in family planning clinics?

options.A: It is legally required before a patient can purchase over-the-counter condoms
options.B: It permanently prevents users from ever changing their chosen method
options.C: It helps clients choose a method that suits their lifestyle while addressing fears or myths
options.D: It replaces the need for any physical health assessment by a doctor

explanation: You nailed it! Good counseling clears up rumors about side effects and helps clients find the contraceptive method that best fits their personal life.

question: At which stage of the family life cycle do parents adjust to the birth of their first infant?

options.A: Childbearing family stage
options.B: Launching center stage
options.C: Beginning family stage
options.D: Aging family stage

explanation: The childbearing stage starts right when that first baby arrives, bringing brand new joys and sleepless nights!

question: What is the chief complaint in a patient health history?

options.A: The nurse's official medical diagnosis
options.B: The results of the patient's blood work
options.C: The main reason the patient is seeking care
options.D: A list of all medications taken in the past year

explanation: The chief complaint captures the primary problem or symptom that brought the patient to the hospital or clinic. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of triage during a mass casualty incident?

options.A: To distribute financial relief funds to displaced families
options.B: To sort patients based on injury severity to prioritize critical care
options.C: To register patients for national health insurance policies
options.D: To assess structural damage to hospital buildings

explanation: Triage lets nurses and doctors quickly assess victims so that those with life-threatening injuries get treated first. You'll master this in clinicals! [learn more](GNS315_U1_T9#GNS315_U1_T9_h8)

question: What is the primary function of carbohydrates in the human body?

options.A: To build strong bones and teeth
options.B: To transport oxygen in the blood
options.C: To provide the body's primary and most efficient source of energy
options.D: To repair damaged skin tissue

explanation: Carbohydrates break down into glucose, which fuels the brain, organs, and muscles for daily activities. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T005#GNS227_U1_T005_h2)

question: A patient is admitted to the ward with severe dehydration and a dry, cracked tongue. What primary mechanical function of the tongue is most likely impaired?

options.A: Directly absorbing simple sugars directly through the taste buds
options.B: Moving and shaping food into a smooth bolus for swallowing
options.C: Filtering dust particles away from the lower respiratory airway
options.D: Producing the primary digestive enzymes needed for starch breakdown

explanation: Dehydration affects oral tissues, making it hard for the tongue to move and moisten food properly into a smooth bolus. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T1#GNS121_U1_T1_h3)

question: When is the final routine post-natal visit usually scheduled to ensure the reproductive organs have fully recovered?

options.A: After one year
options.B: At 24 hours
options.C: On day 3
options.D: Between 4 and 6 weeks

explanation: The 4 to 6-week mark wraps up the puerperium! It's the perfect time for you to confirm the womb has gone back to normal size and chat about family planning.

question: Which side effect of opioids do patients almost NEVER build a tolerance to?

options.A: Nausea
options.B: Constipation
options.C: Dizziness
options.D: Sedation

explanation: Patients get used to the sleepiness and dizziness over time, but opioids keep slowing down the bowels. Always plan ahead with laxatives!

question: What is a classic sign that a patient developed a pneumothorax after a thoracentesis?

options.A: Swelling and redness around the patient's ankles
options.B: Sudden severe pain radiating down the left arm
options.C: Sudden shortness of breath and absent breath sounds on one side
options.D: A high fever with productive green sputum and chills

explanation: Great clinical eye! If air leaks into the chest, it causes the lung to pull away, leading to sudden trouble breathing and quiet breath sounds on that side.

question: What is the main task of cytotoxic T-cells?

options.A: Producing free-floating antibodies in the blood plasma
options.B: Destroying infected or cancerous body cells directly
options.C: Filtering waste materials out of the lymphatic fluid
options.D: Producing new red blood cells inside the bone marrow

explanation: Cytotoxic T-cells are the body's direct hit squad—they spot infected or abnormal cells and destroy them.

question: What is a stakeholder in the healthcare system?

options.A: Any person or group with an interest in health outcomes
options.B: The official paper document given to discharged patients
options.C: A surgical tool used for clamping major blood vessels
options.D: A government tax paid strictly for malaria treatment

explanation: Stakeholders include anyone affected by or capable of influencing health policies, from patients to multinational drug companies. [learn more](GST321_U6_T3#GST321_U6_T3_h2)

question: What happens when a quality improvement project is launched without proper resources or support?

options.A: The hospital automatically gets federal grant money
options.B: Doctors take over all nursing documentation
options.C: Staff experience severe frustration and burnout, leading to project failure
options.D: Patients recover instantly with zero complications

explanation: Right! Without tools, time, and backing, new projects just pile extra stress onto already exhausted nurses. Support is everything.

question: What does a black, tarry stool sample usually tell you about your patient?

options.A: Bleeding in the upper gastrointestinal tract
options.B: Bleeding in the lower rectum or anus
options.C: Severe dehydration and low fluid intake
options.D: A high intake of green leafy vegetables

explanation: As blood travels all the way from the stomach through the gut, digestive juices break it down, turning it dark and tarry by the time it comes out.

question: What is a major risk when a patient takes herbal supplements along with their regular prescription drugs?

options.A: Herbs always neutralize all side effects of drugs
options.B: Adverse drug-nutrient or herb-drug interactions
options.C: The prescription drugs will become completely odorless
options.D: The medications will instantly turn into sugar

explanation: Herbs are active chemicals too! When mixed with hospital drugs, they can sometimes clash, making the drugs too strong or blocking them from working.

question: During which stage of group development do members first experience friction and personality clashes?

options.A: Norming
options.B: Performing
options.C: Storming
options.D: Forming

explanation: The storming stage is marked by disagreements and tension as members push against boundaries and test each other's styles. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T13#GNS124_U5_T13_h2)

question: What happens if a nurse manager ignores a small workplace disagreement?

options.A: It will automatically resolve itself over time.
options.B: It can grow into a major crisis that threatens patient safety.
options.C: It will improve overall staff productivity.
options.D: It will make doctors respect nurses more.

explanation: Unresolved issues fester and ruin teamwork, which can sadly put patient care in danger. Good to know!

question: A nurse accidentally drops and breaks an old mercury blood pressure machine on the ward floor. What kind of hazard is this?

options.A: Chemical hazard
options.B: Biological hazard
options.C: Genotoxic hazard
options.D: Radioactive hazard

explanation: Mercury is a toxic heavy metal, making it a chemical hazard. Its vapors can easily be breathed in or absorbed through the skin if not cleaned up properly!

question: Why is a little bit of moulding considered a normal and helpful thing during birth?

options.A: It prevents the baby from breathing too early
options.B: It permanently seals the cranial sutures closed
options.C: It speeds up the dilation of the maternal cervix
options.D: It helps reduce the head dimensions to fit the pelvis

explanation: Spot on! By letting the bones telescope just a little bit, the baby's head safely adapts to the curves of the birth canal.

question: What colour and flow pattern does arterial bleeding typically show?

options.A: Bright red and trickling evenly
options.B: Bright red and spurting in jets
options.C: Dark red and oozing slowly
options.D: Dark red and flowing in a steady stream

explanation: Arteries carry oxygenated blood under high pressure from the heart, causing it to spurt out in pulses when a vessel is cut. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T2#GNS112_U7_T2_h1)

question: Why must nurses understand basic inventory and stock control principles?

options.A: To design new storage shelves for the hospital
options.B: To negotiate better prices with medical suppliers
options.C: To take over the job of the hospital pharmacist
options.D: To prevent emergency supply shortages on the ward

explanation: Nurses handle ward supplies every day, so knowing stock rules helps them prevent running out of critical items during patient care. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h1)

question: Why is infection control often trickier in a patient's home compared to a hospital ward?

options.A: Standard precautions are legally prohibited in private residences
options.B: The environment is dynamic and outside direct professional control
options.C: Clients in homes always carry more dangerous bacteria
options.D: Hospitals lack the sanitation resources found in households

explanation: Every home is different! Unlike a controlled hospital room, you have family members, pets, and unique layouts to navigate. Keep up the great thinking!

question: Which of these is NOT a common sign of meningitis?

options.A: High fever and body chills
options.B: Sudden complete paralysis of the lower limbs
options.C: Severe and pounding headache
options.D: Stiff and painful neck movement

explanation: Spot on! Meningitis causes terrible headaches, fever, and a stiff neck, but leg paralysis is not a standard sign of the infection.

question: What is usually the very first step when preparing to study a community?

options.A: Writing the final evaluation report for the ministry of health
options.B: Administering mass vaccinations to all school children
options.C: Gaining entry and building trust with local community leaders
options.D: Purchasing expensive medical equipment for the local clinic

explanation: Before collecting data, nurses must respect local protocols and gain the cooperation of community leaders to ensure participation. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a current challenge facing community health nurses in Nigeria?

options.A: Funding shortages for public health programs
options.B: Infrastructural deficits in rural clinics
options.C: The double burden of infectious and non-communicable diseases
options.D: Zero prevalence of any health problems in the country

explanation: You got it! Nigeria definitely still deals with various health challenges, so saying there are zero problems isn't true.

question: What is 'problem-focused coping' when dealing with a health challenge?

options.A: Blaming other people for causing the physical disability
options.B: Taking direct action to change or fix the stressful situation
options.C: Ignoring the problem completely until it goes away
options.D: Relying entirely on denial and emotional shutdown

explanation: Correct! It's all about practical steps—like learning new skills or modifying the home to handle challenges head-on.

question: How is palliative care different from traditional hospice care when it comes to timing?

options.A: Palliative care starts only after curative treatment stops
options.B: Hospice care is started immediately upon a chronic diagnosis
options.C: Palliative care can be given alongside life-prolonging treatments
options.D: Hospice care avoids all medications except pain relievers

explanation: Unlike hospice, which is strictly for end-of-life care, palliative care can begin right at diagnosis while the patient is still receiving active treatments to cure them. Great job working through this!

question: What is the main goal of public health agencies, as opposed to a regular hospital ward?

options.A: Managing health at a population level
options.B: Training medical doctors exclusively
options.C: Manufacturing pharmaceutical drugs
options.D: Providing surgical operations only

explanation: You've got this! While hospital wards focus on one sick patient at a time, public health agencies look at the big picture—keeping whole communities healthy and preventing disease.

question: A mother asks what food to first give her six-month-old. What is the best nurse response?

options.A: Cow milk straight from the carton to build strong bones
options.B: Clear vegetable broths with added table salt for taste
options.C: Sweetened fruit juices to encourage quick swallowing
options.D: Thick, nutrient-dense mashed foods like iron-fortified porridge or yam

explanation: First foods should be thick and rich in nutrients, especially iron, to match the rapid growth spurt of a six-month-old baby.

question: How do bile salts help your body digest fats?

options.A: Breaking large fat globules into tiny emulsified droplets
options.B: Releasing digestive enzymes directly into the fat droplets
options.C: Neutralizing stomach acid before fats reach the intestine
options.D: Chemically dissolving fats into simple fatty acids

explanation: Bile salts act just like dish soap, turning big globs of fat into tiny droplets so digestive enzymes can easily reach them.

question: What is the main job of hormones in our bodies?

options.A: Generate rapid electrical impulses for muscle contraction
options.B: Transport oxygen molecules from the lungs to body tissues
options.C: Filter waste products directly out of the bloodstream
options.D: Act as chemical messengers to regulate target organs

explanation: Think of hormones as chemical text messages sent through the blood to tell different organs what to do. You've got this!

question: Why is maintaining a patient's mobility considered vital for overall health?

options.A: It shortens the required hospital stay to one day
options.B: It guarantees complete recovery from any surgery
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for pain medication
options.D: It supports circulation and preserves muscle mass

explanation: Movement keeps blood flowing properly and prevents muscles from weakening quickly during illness or recovery. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T8#GNS324_U3_T8_h1)

question: At what point should health care waste be segregated?

options.A: After the cleaning staff transport it outside
options.B: At the exact point and time of generation
options.C: Only when the waste bins are completely full
options.D: During the final incineration process

explanation: Segregation must happen immediately where the waste is produced to prevent mixing hazardous and non-hazardous materials. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h3)

question: How does the human ear act like a biological transducer?

options.A: It filters out background noise using chemical barriers
options.B: It converts mechanical air vibrations into electrical nerve signals
options.C: It amplifies light waves into visual images in the brain
options.D: It stores sound energy inside the fluid of the middle ear

explanation: Transduction simply means changing one form of energy into another. The ear takes physical sound waves moving through the air and translates them into electrical messages your brain can understand.

question: Which of these is a key intervention used by modern psychiatric nurses?

options.A: Strict physical confinement in isolated cells
options.B: Performing major neurosurgical operations independently
options.C: Therapeutic communication and psychoeducation
options.D: Withholding food to enforce behavioral change

explanation: You nailed it! Modern psychiatric nursing is built on comforting conversation, teaching patients and families, and managing medications safely—no more harsh punishments.

question: Which of these nursing actions is a classic example of primary prevention?

options.A: Managing blood pressure medications for hypertension
options.B: Screening adult patients for elevated blood glucose
options.C: Providing physical therapy after a stroke occurs
options.D: Administering the measles vaccine to school children

explanation: Spot on! Primary prevention stops a disease before it even gets the chance to start. Giving vaccines is the best way to shield healthy people.

question: A patient is completely bedridden from a muscle disorder. Which bone problem are they most at risk for?

options.A: Sudden overproduction of red blood cells
options.B: Pathological bone fractures from decreased density
options.C: Involuntary muscle hypertrophy in the lower limbs
options.D: Drastic permanent height gain from spinal decompression

explanation: Bones need weight and pressure to stay strong. Staying in bed stops that pressure, making bones weak and fragile.

question: Which of the following structures is part of the axial region?

options.A: The upper arm
options.B: The hands
options.C: The trunk
options.D: The lower leg

explanation: The axial region includes the head, neck, and trunk, while the limbs make up the appendicular region. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T4#GNS111_U1_T4_h2)

question: A mother insists on keeping her baby's heavy winter jacket on during weighing. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Record the weight with the jacket and note it as the true weight
options.B: Explain gently that the jacket must be removed for an accurate weight
options.C: Weigh the baby with the jacket and subtract an estimated guess
options.D: Refuse to weigh the baby until the next clinic visit

explanation: Heavy clothing adds significant extra weight, so infants should be weighed naked or with minimal clothing like a dry diaper. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T8#GNS225_U2_T8_h4)

question: Why is it risky to give a patient an unmixed suspension right from the bottle?

options.A: The liquid will foam up and block the patient's airway
options.B: The patient might get a weak dose first and a toxic dose last
options.C: The medicine will taste too sweet and cause vomiting
options.D: The solid particles will react chemically with stomach acid

explanation: Spot on! Since the medicine settles at the bottom, an unmixed bottle means watery liquid at first (weak dose) and a sludgy finish at the end (too strong!).

question: A researcher wants to show how blood pressure readings changed across four different clinic visits for a group of patients. Which format should they choose?

options.A: A graph
options.B: A qualitative interview transcript
options.C: A dense text paragraph
options.D: A demographic listing

explanation: Graphs are the best format for illustrating trends and changes across multiple time points, like clinic visits. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T4#GNS224_U2_T4_h2)

question: What is a major benefit of putting a newborn straight onto the mother's chest for skin-to-skin contact?

options.A: It stabilizes the infant's body temperature and heart rate
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for vitamin K injections
options.C: It speeds up the closure of the umbilical cord vessels
options.D: It prevents the occurrence of physiological jaundice

explanation: Mum's chest is like a natural incubator! It helps steady the baby's breathing, heart rate, and keeps them nice and warm.

question: Which vital sign must a nurse check right before giving an IV opioid?

options.A: Capillary refill
options.B: Respiratory rate
options.C: Body temperature
options.D: Oxygen saturation only

explanation: Always check how many breaths the patient is taking per minute. Opioids can dangerously slow down breathing.

question: Which group makes up the largest number of paid workers in Nigerian primary health centers?

options.A: Pharmacist Specialists
options.B: Laboratory Pathologists
options.C: Consultant Paediatricians
options.D: Community Health Extension Workers

explanation: Spot on! Community Health Extension Workers (CHEWs) form the backbone of our primary health centers, working tirelessly on the frontlines.

question: What is the main goal of the 'sensitivity' part of a urine culture and sensitivity (C&S) test?

options.A: To determine which antibiotics will kill the specific bacteria
options.B: To measure the exact volume of urine produced in 24 hours
options.C: To calculate the patient's specific gravity and hydration status
options.D: To check if red blood cells are fragile under chemical stress

explanation: The sensitivity test is like a test-run for medicines! It shows us which exact antibiotic will successfully knock out the patient's specific infection.

question: What is a key requirement for valid informed consent regarding medication administration?

options.A: The doctor orders the drug without explaining side effects
options.B: The client agrees voluntarily after understanding the risks and benefits
options.C: The family signs the paperwork without telling the patient
options.D: The nurse makes the final decision for the patient

explanation: Informed consent requires voluntary agreement built on a clear understanding of what the medication does and what side effects might occur. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T3#GNS125_U3_T3_h5)

question: What is the very first step in conceptualizing a research study?

options.A: Discharging patients who fit the study criteria
options.B: Identifying a specific clinical problem or topic
options.C: Submitting the final paper to a medical journal
options.D: Purchasing expensive data analysis software

explanation: A researcher must first pinpoint what issue needs investigating before taking any further steps. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T1#GNS217_U3_T1_h2)

question: What is the primary goal of Post-Abortion Care (PAC) services?

options.A: To diagnose and treat chronic pelvic inflammatory disease
options.B: To reduce maternal death and injury from unsafe abortions
options.C: To promote voluntary surgical sterilization for all women
options.D: To provide routine antenatal checkups for pregnant mothers

explanation: PAC is specifically structured as an emergency and follow-up response to lower the high rates of maternal mortality and morbidity linked to unsafe procedures. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h1)

question: How does the team nursing setup benefit junior staff and nursing students on the ward?

options.A: By exempting them from doing any physical patient care
options.B: By allowing them to write hospital policies
options.C: By giving them a supportive environment to learn from senior leaders
options.D: By forcing them to work alone without any supervision

explanation: That's right! Working closely with a registered nurse team leader gives students safe guidance and wonderful practical experience. Every shift is a learning win!

question: Why is it super important for nurses in primary health clinics to know about cancer?

options.A: Primary health centers run all national chemotherapy programs
options.B: Infectious diseases are no longer treated in Nigeria
options.C: Community clinics handle complex surgeries daily
options.D: Nurses are usually the first health workers patients see with early symptoms

explanation: Spotting early signs at the grass-roots level means we can refer patients quickly and save lives. Great nursing starts in the community!

question: Which vitamin helps the body absorb plant-based iron much better?

options.A: Vitamin E
options.B: Vitamin D
options.C: Vitamin C
options.D: Vitamin K

explanation: Taking vitamin C alongside plant-based iron sources significantly improves how well the gut absorbs the mineral. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T15#GNS311_U2_T15_h2)

question: Which dangerous practice with used needles should every nurse avoid completely?

options.A: Carrying sharps boxes on a trolley
options.B: Dropping syringes into yellow bins
options.C: Recapping used needles by hand
options.D: Checking fill lines on containers

explanation: Never try to recap a needle with your hands! It's one of the leading causes of accidental needle-stick injuries in nursing.

question: How does actively absorbing sodium from the gut affect fluid movement?

options.A: It destroys water molecules to prevent severe dehydration
options.B: It draws water out of the lumen and into the mucosal cells
options.C: It repels water molecules and forces them into the stool
options.D: It keeps water trapped inside the lumen until digestion finishes

explanation: Exactly! Pumping sodium out of the gut space creates an osmotic pull that drags water right along with it into the body tissues.

question: Which major part of the adult brain develops directly from the telencephalon?

options.A: Cerebrum
options.B: Pons
options.C: Thalamus
options.D: Medulla oblongata

explanation: The telencephalon is the part of the early brain that grows and expands to form our large cerebrum and its two halves.

question: Why should outbreak control measures sometimes start before lab results are fully finalized?

options.A: To avoid paperwork and administrative meetings
options.B: Because laboratory tests are always completely inaccurate
options.C: Because doctors are not allowed to read lab reports
options.D: To prevent further spread and save lives immediately

explanation: Waiting for lab work during a fast-moving crisis can cost lives. Taking action early based on clinical signs is a lifesaver!

question: At what age is the initial virological diagnostic test (DNA PCR) recommended for an HIV-exposed infant?

options.A: At 6 weeks of age or earliest possible contact
options.B: Immediately upon delivery before leaving the labor ward
options.C: At 18 months of age after breastfeeding completely stops
options.D: At 5 years of age before starting primary school

explanation: DNA PCR testing is recommended around 6 weeks of age to detect the genetic material of the virus early and start treatment if positive. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h6)

question: Why is it super important for nurses to know the generic name of a drug?

options.A: It is the only name recognized by hospital billing departments
options.B: It remains universal and prevents confusion across different manufacturing companies
options.C: It tells the nurse the exact physical shape and color of the pill
options.D: It automatically guarantees the drug is more affordable for the patient

explanation: You nailed it. Generic names stay the same everywhere, saving us from company name confusion!

question: Which Nigerian law sets the main minimum standards for factory safety and worker welfare?

options.A: The National Health Insurance Act
options.B: The Land Use Act
options.C: The Criminal Code Act
options.D: The Factories Act

explanation: You'll see this often in Nigerian public health! The Factories Act is the key law that protects workers and regulates safety conditions in Nigerian workplaces.

question: An infusion pump starts beeping with a 'downstream occlusion' alarm. What should you check first?

options.A: The software version installed on the pump display
options.B: The IV tubing for kinks, closed clamps, or blockages
options.C: The main hospital electrical breaker panel in the hallway
options.D: The expiration date printed on the primary medication bag

explanation: That's correct! 'Downstream' means between the pump and the patient. Always check the line first for bends, pinches, or a closed roller clamp.

question: How does a global body like the International Council of Nurses (ICN) differ from a local national association?

options.A: The ICN writes the specific nursing school curricula for every country
options.B: The ICN manages local salary disputes for individual clinics
options.C: The ICN directly licenses nurses to work in specific hospitals
options.D: The ICN federates national associations to address global health issues

explanation: While national bodies look at local laws, the ICN brings different countries together to tackle worldwide challenges like nursing shortages and global health policies.

question: Why is it best to look for local strengths in the community before asking for outside donations?

options.A: External organizations refuse to work with community nurses
options.B: Local materials are always completely free of charge
options.C: Outside donors are legally banned from helping health clinics
options.D: It builds self-reliance so the program can keep running long-term

explanation: Spot on! Using local assets empowers the community so the project doesn't collapse the moment outside help stops.

question: What causes the first heart sound, commonly heard as 'lub'?

options.A: Opening of the aortic valve
options.B: Closing of the semilunar valves
options.C: Blood rushing into the atria
options.D: Closing of the AV valves

explanation: The first heart sound (S1) is produced when the tricuspid and mitral valves snap shut at the start of ventricular contraction. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h6)

question: What exactly is colostrum?

options.A: The thick, yellowish first breast milk produced after birth
options.B: The primary protein supplement used to treat severe malnutrition
options.C: A local porridge made from fermented yellow maize
options.D: A traditional herbal drink given to calm crying babies

explanation: Colostrum is the super-nutritious, antibody-rich milk that comes right after delivery. Sadly, bad taboos sometimes cause mothers to throw it away—good thing you know better!

question: Why do some joints in our body, like the ones in the skull, not move at all?

options.A: To help pump blood through the skeletal system
options.B: To store extra calcium for the growing skeleton
options.C: To provide protection for underlying organs
options.D: To allow muscles to attach more firmly to bone

explanation: Spot on! Immovable joints act like a solid helmet, keeping delicate organs like your brain safe and sound.

question: Giving routine childhood immunizations is an example of which level of prevention?

options.A: Quaternary prevention
options.B: Secondary prevention
options.C: Tertiary prevention
options.D: Primary prevention

explanation: Fantastic! Vaccines stop diseases from ever happening in the first place, which is the definition of primary prevention.

question: Why do nurses often recommend simple activities like brisk walking instead of expensive gyms?

options.A: Gyms are strictly illegal in most rural Nigerian communities
options.B: Walking burns zero calories compared to gym equipment
options.C: Outdoor exercise is the only way to build muscle strength
options.D: It encourages long-term adherence by fitting into everyday life

explanation: You got it! Affordable and practical activities are much easier for people to keep doing consistently over time without getting stressed.

question: A family wants to eat healthily on a modest budget in Nigeria. Which purchasing approach is best?

options.A: Purchasing only imported cereals and canned soups
options.B: Buying expensive pre-packaged meals from supermarkets
options.C: Avoiding local open markets entirely
options.D: Buying local whole foods like beans, vegetables, and tubers

explanation: Local whole foods provide essential nutrients affordably without the high markups of processed imported goods. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T006#GNS227_U3_T006_h7)

question: Which lab test is most commonly used to confirm a Lassa virus infection?

options.A: Microscopic stool examination for ova
options.B: Sputum acid-fast bacilli smear
options.C: Electrocardiogram rhythm strip
options.D: Reverse Transcription-Polymerase Chain Reaction (RT-PCR)

explanation: RT-PCR checks for viral RNA in the blood with great accuracy, making it the gold standard for confirmation.

question: Why should a quality improvement team always include someone working right on the hospital floor?

options.A: To secure funding grants for new medical equipment purchases
options.B: To handle all communication with hospital executive management
options.C: To replace the team leader when meetings run too late
options.D: To provide real-world feedback on how changes affect daily workflow

explanation: Spot on! Frontline staff make sure that new ideas are actually realistic and practical for the nurses and aides doing the work every day.

question: Why is careful monitoring of IV fluids especially vital during labor for a mother with kidney disease?

options.A: Excess fluids stop the uterus from contracting normally after the baby is born
options.B: Compromised kidneys cannot handle fluid overload, increasing the risk of pulmonary edema
options.C: Too much intravenous fluid causes the infant's kidneys to stop working permanently
options.D: Intravenous fluids react badly with standard pain medications used in labor

explanation: Weakened kidneys can't get rid of extra water well, so giving too much IV fluid can cause it to back right up into her lungs.

question: A stroke damages the motor tracts on the right side of a patient's brain. Where will they likely show physical weakness?

options.A: Exclusively in the respiratory diaphragm
options.B: Only in the facial muscles on the right side
options.C: Equally on both sides of the entire body
options.D: On the left side of the body

explanation: Because our motor pathways cross over to the opposite side, brain damage on the right side causes weakness on the left side of the body. Classic nursing neurology!

question: A clinic finds out that working mothers miss immunizations because clinics close too early. What should the nurse manager do?

options.A: Adjust clinic operating hours to accommodate working parents
options.B: Stop collecting data on clinic attendance times completely
options.C: Blame the mothers for lacking commitment to child health
options.D: Reduce the total number of vaccines offered at the facility

explanation: When evaluation points out a problem like inconvenient timing, we adapt our services—like tweaking clinic hours—to help working parents out.

question: Which drug class works by acting as faulty building blocks that trick the reverse transcriptase enzyme?

options.A: Integrase Inhibitors
options.B: Nucleoside Reverse Transcriptase Inhibitors (NRTIs)
options.C: Entry Inhibitors
options.D: Protease Inhibitors (PIs)

explanation: Well done! NRTIs send in fake building blocks. The virus gets tricked into using them, which completely halts the creation of its viral DNA.

question: Which dimension of quality care is all about protecting patients from accidental injuries and infections?

options.A: Efficiency
options.B: Timeliness
options.C: Equity
options.D: Safety

explanation: Safety is all about protecting your patients. It means keeping medical errors and hospital-acquired infections far away from them! [learn more](GNS312_U5_T2#GNS312_U5_T2_h2)

question: How would you best describe peristalsis?

options.A: Wave-like muscle contractions that push food forward
options.B: Localized churning that mixes food in the small intestine
options.C: The absorption of water through the large bowel wall
options.D: The secretion of digestive enzymes by the pancreas

explanation: Spot on! Think of peristalsis like a wave of muscle squeezes moving food steadily along down the digestive tube.

question: What is the main reason for nursing supervision in the hospital ward?

options.A: To ensure care meets safe and ethical standards
options.B: To discipline staff who make clinical errors
options.C: To reduce the number of working hours for nurses
options.D: To replace formal classroom nursing education

explanation: Think of supervision as a supportive guide. Its main job is to make sure patient care stays safe, proper, and of high quality!

question: How do common hormonal contraceptives (like pills and injectables) mainly prevent pregnancy?

options.A: By suppressing ovulation and thickening cervical mucus
options.B: By killing the ovum before fertilization can take place
options.C: By permanently closing the fallopian tubes with scar tissue
options.D: By physically destroying sperm inside the vaginal canal

explanation: Hormones trick the body into holding back the egg (no ovulation) and make the cervical mucus too thick for swimming sperm to get through. Clever, right?

question: What does Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR) actually measure?

options.A: The total calories burned during heavy physical exercise
options.B: The energy needed to maintain basic life functions at rest
options.C: The amount of heat produced during food digestion
options.D: The maximum oxygen consumption during endurance training

explanation: Think of BMR as your body's idle speed. It's the bare minimum energy required to keep your heart pumping, lungs breathing, and organs working while you do absolutely nothing.

question: Why can a problem at the very start of hormone production affect multiple different hormone levels?

options.A: All sex hormones share a common pathway originating from cholesterol.
options.B: Adrenal glands stop producing blood entirely.
options.C: Receptors on target tissues become permanently blocked.
options.D: The liver destroys excess hormones when one pathway fails.

explanation: Since all sex hormones branch out from the same starting block (cholesterol), a hiccup early in the chain reaction alters everything downstream. Makes total sense when you picture it like a branching river!

question: What do we call large cells with multiple nuclei formed when virus-infected cells fuse together?

options.A: Neutrophils
options.B: Granulomas
options.C: Syncytia
options.D: Abscesses

explanation: Syncytia are giant multi-nucleated cells created when certain clever viruses trick neighboring cell membranes into melting together.

question: How does the complement system mainly attack invading bacteria?

options.A: By producing thick mucus in the airways
options.B: By lowering body temperature to slow down germs
options.C: By binding directly to viral RNA
options.D: By poking holes in bacterial cell membranes to make them burst

explanation: Complement proteins team up to punch tiny holes right through the cell walls of invading bacteria, causing them to burst open.

question: Which simple home modification helps prevent dangerous tripping hazards for someone using a walker?

options.A: Removing loose throw rugs from the floors
options.B: Adding decorative floor mats near doorways
options.C: Waxing hardwood floors until they shine
options.D: Placing heavy wooden furniture in hallways

explanation: Loose throw rugs easily bunch up under mobility aids like walkers and wheel tips, creating a major fall hazard. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T9#GNS225_U5_T9_h5)

question: Why do nurses promote local foods during cooking demos instead of imported ones?

options.A: Local health policies legally forbid the use of foreign recipes
options.B: Local ingredients are usually more affordable and accessible to the community
options.C: Imported foods cause immediate illness in all age groups
options.D: Imported foods are always completely devoid of any nutritional value

explanation: Spot on! Good nutrition teaching has to be practical. Using foods that families can easily buy or grow nearby ensures the habit sticks.

question: If a student wants to study how hospital room ventilation and fresh air affect patient healing, which theory fits best?

options.A: Callista Roy’s Adaptation Model
options.B: Dorothea Orem’s Self-Care Deficit Theory
options.C: Florence Nightingale’s Environmental Theory
options.D: Madeleine Leininger’s Culture Care Theory

explanation: You nailed it! Nightingale was the pioneer of using clean air, light, and a healthy environment to help patients recover.

question: Which nerve brings the parasympathetic signals that make the bladder contract when you want to pee?

options.A: Pudendal nerve
options.B: Obturator nerve
options.C: Hypogastric nerve
options.D: Pelvic nerve

explanation: Spot on! The pelvic nerve carries those important parasympathetic signals that tell the detrusor muscle to squeeze and empty the bladder.

question: How does a copper IUD mainly prevent pregnancy?

options.A: By releasing high doses of estrogen to stop ovulation
options.B: By swelling the cervix shut so sperm cannot enter
options.C: By physically blocking the Fallopian tubes with wire
options.D: By releasing copper ions that stun and damage sperm cells

explanation: The copper creates an environment that sperm really hate. It damages them and stops them from ever reaching the egg!

question: What does a drug's half-life represent in pharmacokinetics?

options.A: The time it takes for the body to absorb half of an oral dose
options.B: The time it takes for blood concentration of the drug to decrease by 50 percent
options.C: The exact number of hours a drug remains active in the stomach
options.D: The time required for the liver to metabolize half of the active ingredient

explanation: Half-life measures how long it takes for the amount of drug in the blood to drop down to half of its previous level. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T4#GNS125_U5_T4_h6)

question: A patient stops shaking after a seizure, falls into a deep, snoring sleep, and feels confused when woken up. What nursing term describes this phase?

options.A: Aura phase
options.B: Tonic phase
options.C: Postictal phase
options.D: Clonic phase

explanation: Great job! 'Post' means after, and 'ictal' refers to the seizure. This recovery period is the postictal phase.

question: What is the ultimate aim of a community health nurse in mobilisation?

options.A: Building local capacity so the community runs its own health programs
options.B: Collecting data to publish research papers in medical journals
options.C: Making sure the local clinic receives a large budget from abroad
options.D: Ensuring the nurse becomes the most respected person in the village

explanation: The goal of community mobilisation is self-reliance, where locals have the skills to manage their health without constant outside intervention. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h8)

question: Which of these is an example of indirect gender discrimination in a community?

options.A: Refusing to treat a patient based on their sex
options.B: A sign on a clinic door stating men cannot enter
options.C: Paying female nurses less than male nurses for the same job
options.D: Clinic hours that conflict with domestic caregiving duties

explanation: Indirect discrimination happens when a rule looks fair to everyone on paper, but actually makes it hard for one specific group to get care. You are building strong community nursing knowledge!

question: A nurse wants to start a health program in a village. When should community participation ideally begin?

options.A: When the government evaluates the final report
options.B: After the foreign funding runs out completely
options.C: From the very beginning during problem identification
options.D: Only when the clinic building is finished

explanation: True participation starts at the planning stage so the community actually helps identify what needs fixing. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T1#GNS124_U4_T1_h2)

question: Which medication group is most commonly given via nebulizer to relax tightened airway muscles?

options.A: Vasopressors
options.B: Anticoagulants
options.C: Antibiotics
options.D: Bronchodilators

explanation: Bronchodilators open up constricted breathing tubes so air can flow freely in and out of the lungs. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h2)

question: What is a nurse leader's best first move when handling a disagreement between community groups?

options.A: Suspend the health program until everyone calms down
options.B: Report all complaining members to the local police
options.C: Ignore the tension because arguments always resolve themselves
options.D: Listen to all sides and look for common ground

explanation: Active listening and finding shared interests help calm the tension and bring people together. You're building great leadership skills!

question: Which medical gases are usually piped right into the walls of an operating room?

options.A: Compressed steam and cooking gas
options.B: Methane, nitrogen, and propane
options.C: Carbon dioxide, helium, and hydrogen
options.D: Oxygen, nitrous oxide, and medical air

explanation: Correct! Wall pipelines supply essential life-support and anesthetic gases directly so the team always has what they need.

question: Why is using a standard checklist or form important when reviewing old patient charts?

options.A: It automatically prevents all forms of patient bias
options.B: It ensures every chart is checked for the same consistent variables
options.C: It allows the researcher to change the research question midway
options.D: It replaces the need for ethical approval from the hospital

explanation: Exactly! Using a standard form keeps your data collection neat, uniform, and organized, even when you're looking through hundreds of different patient folders.

question: What is the main purpose of secondary prevention?

options.A: Rehabilitation after a permanent disability occurs
options.B: Preventing a healthy person from ever getting sick
options.C: Early diagnosis and prompt treatment of a disease
options.D: Creating broad national economic health policies

explanation: Secondary prevention is all about catching issues early through screening before severe symptoms take over. Spot it early, treat it early!

question: Why must nurse supervisors make sure staff stay strictly within their scope of practice?

options.A: To prevent professional misconduct and protect patient safety
options.B: To reduce the financial cost of running the hospital ward
options.C: To make sure doctors do not have to do any ward work
options.D: To speed up the promotion process for junior nurses

explanation: Knowing your scope keeps patients safe from harm and protects you legally from stepping outside your training.

question: Besides basic nutrition science, what strongly shapes what people eat every day?

options.A: Recommendations from distant pharmaceutical companies
options.B: Strict international food export regulations
options.C: Cultural heritage, religious traditions, and socioeconomic status
options.D: Global shipping schedules and fuel prices

explanation: You got it! What we put on our plates is deeply tied to our culture, traditions, pocket, and generational habits.

question: Which joint is most likely to suffer first when a patient has a sudden gout attack?

options.A: The hip joint
options.B: The elbow joint
options.C: The shoulder joint
options.D: The big toe

explanation: Great job! The base of the big toe is the classic hotspot for a first-time gout attack. Because of cooler body temperatures there and normal daily pressure, uric acid loves to form crystals in this spot first.

question: Which of the following is an example of a long-acting reversible contraceptive method?

options.A: A subdermal hormonal implant
options.B: A packet of daily oral contraceptive pills
options.C: Spermicidal foam applied before sex
options.D: Male latex condoms used during intercourse

explanation: Implants and intrauterine devices are classified as LARC methods because they work continuously for years without daily action from the user. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h4)

question: What is a major downside of relying only on authority figures for your clinical decisions?

options.A: Institutional leaders have no clinical background
options.B: Authority figures are impossible to locate in a hospital
options.C: Senior nurses refuse to speak with junior staff
options.D: Experts may base views on custom rather than evidence

explanation: Even experienced experts can fall back on outdated habits if their views aren't backed by solid, current research.

question: What is the main goal of rehabilitation in nursing care?

options.A: To completely cure chronic underlying pathologies
options.B: To eliminate the need for any follow-up care
options.C: To maximize a person's independence and functional level
options.D: To keep patients admitted in hospital wards long-term

explanation: You've got this! Rehab is all about helping your patients live life to the fullest and do as much for themselves as possible, even if a chronic condition is still there.

question: Which of the following is a key frontline responsibility of a reproductive health nurse?

options.A: Providing antenatal care and family planning counseling
options.B: Conducting biomedical laboratory research
options.C: Purchasing medical equipment for the entire hospital
options.D: Drafting national health insurance policies

explanation: Frontline reproductive health nurses directly provide services like antenatal monitoring, labor support, and contraceptive counseling. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T1#GNS312_U5_T1_h5)

question: Which of the following is an example of an adaptive coping mechanism for a newly diagnosed HIV patient?

options.A: Turning to heavy alcohol use to forget the diagnosis
options.B: Denying the existence of the virus and skipping clinic visits
options.C: Joining a peer support group and talking with a counsellor
options.D: Isolating oneself completely from all human contact

explanation: Seeking community support and professional guidance helps patients process their diagnosis in a healthy, constructive manner. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T8#GNS216_U6_T8_h7)

question: Why are children with acute osteomyelitis at risk for long-term bone growth issues?

options.A: Bones in children never fully heal once inflamed
options.B: Antibiotics used in pediatrics actively dissolve healthy cartilage
options.C: Children lack any ability to form new bone after an infection
options.D: The infection can damage nearby growth plates, altering future bone growth

explanation: Kids are still growing! If an infection spreads into their growth plates (epiphyseal plates), it can mess with how that bone grows as they get older.

question: Which medication is a core part of the preferred first-line ART treatment for adults in Nigeria?

options.A: Paracetamol
options.B: Dolutegravir
options.C: Insulin
options.D: Penicillin

explanation: Correct! Dolutegravir is a powerful, safe integrase inhibitor that forms the backbone of standard first-line HIV treatment in Nigeria today.

question: What is the main job of UNOCHA during an international crisis?

options.A: Directly manufacturing and distributing pharmaceutical drugs
options.B: Coordinating humanitarian relief efforts among multiple organizations
options.C: Training local nurses in bedside clinical procedures
options.D: Providing armed military defense for disaster zones

explanation: Spot on! UNOCHA acts like the ultimate coordinator, making sure all the different groups rushing to help are working together smoothly.

question: A patient leaks a little urine whenever she coughs or sneezes. Which pelvic floor function has failed here?

options.A: Continence support during increased pressure
options.B: Complete relaxation during bladder emptying
options.C: Core stabilization for the spinal column
options.D: Sexual sensation enhancement

explanation: You got it! This is called stress incontinence—when the pelvic floor isn't strong or fast enough to close the urethra against sudden pressure like a sneeze.

question: What is the main point of doing a Spontaneous Breathing Trial (SBT)?

options.A: To measure the exact size of the patient's lung capacity
options.B: To clean out thick secretions from the lower airways
options.C: To give the mechanical ventilator a chance to rest and cool down
options.D: To test if the patient can breathe without full ventilator support

explanation: An SBT dials back the machine's help to see if the patient's own breathing muscles are ready to take over the job.

question: Which of these is a great environmental change to help a patient with low vision stay safe?

options.A: Using high-contrast colors on stairs and doorway edges
options.B: Placing scattered small rugs across hard floors for comfort
options.C: Keeping furniture rearranged frequently to test spatial memory
options.D: Dimming all indoor lights to prevent harsh eye strain

explanation: High contrast is a lifesaver! Marking steps and door edges clearly helps patients with low vision see boundaries easily and prevents nasty falls.

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier to effective nursing management planning?

options.A: Limited time due to busy daily duties
options.B: Excessive availability of reliable data
options.C: Staff resistance to clinical changes
options.D: Severe shortage of financial resources

explanation: Reliable data helps planning; the barrier is actually a lack of information, not an excess of good data. [learn more](GST321_U1_T5#GST321_U1_T5_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of decontamination in a healthcare setting?

options.A: To ensure that expired drugs are safely disposed of in the incinerator
options.B: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing new medical instruments
options.C: To make hospital wards smell fresh and clean for visitors
options.D: To break the chain of infection and protect patients and staff

explanation: Decontamination removes or destroys harmful microorganisms to stop them from spreading to vulnerable patients and healthcare workers. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h1)

question: How is putting a catheter into a male patient different from a female patient?

options.A: It lacks a sphincter muscle, making insertion completely effortless
options.B: It opens directly into the abdominal cavity
options.C: It is longer and has natural curves that require careful maneuvering
options.D: It is wider, requiring much larger catheter sizes

explanation: Exactly! The male urethra is longer and travels through the prostate, so you have to gently navigate a few natural bends during the procedure.

question: Why are anthropometric measurements so helpful in busy or rural primary healthcare clinics?

options.A: They replace the need for taking a complete medical history
options.B: They are non-invasive, affordable, and simple to perform anywhere
options.C: They require expensive laboratory reagents to process results
options.D: They provide instant diagnosis for all known infectious diseases

explanation: Spot on! Because they need very little equipment and no lab work, you can easily use them during community outreaches or rural postings.

question: Why do sulfonylurea drugs carry a higher risk of causing low blood sugar (hypoglycaemia) compared to Metformin?

options.A: They destroy counter-regulatory hormones like glucagon and cortisol
options.B: They force the kidneys to dump excess sugar into the urine too quickly
options.C: They actively stimulate insulin release from the pancreas regardless of blood sugar levels
options.D: They completely block the liver from releasing any stored glucose ever

explanation: Spot on! Sulfonylureas keep pushing the pancreas to pump out insulin even if blood sugar levels are already dropping, which can cause hypoglycaemia.

question: What is the main job of the appendicular skeleton?

options.A: Maintaining the central structural axis for upright balance
options.B: Protecting the delicate structures of the central nervous system
options.C: Facilitating body movement and interacting with the environment
options.D: Housing the bone marrow that produces white blood cells

explanation: The appendicular skeleton includes your arms, legs, and shoulders—built for moving around and grabbing things!

question: What is the main purpose of performing Leopold's maneuvers during an antenatal visit?

options.A: To check if the mother has a urinary tract infection
options.B: To determine fetal position, size, and presentation
options.C: To measure the exact amount of blood in the body
options.D: To find out when the baby will start walking

explanation: Leopold's maneuvers use gentle hand movements on the abdomen to feel how the baby is lying. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T8#GNS225_U3_T8_h5)

question: A patient with severe liver cirrhosis is most likely to develop which complication due to backed-up portal blood flow?

options.A: High levels of pancreatic enzymes in the mouth
options.B: Ascites or fluid accumulation in the abdominal cavity
options.C: Rapid digestion of dietary fats without any bile
options.D: Excessive production of saliva causing drooling

explanation: When liver scarring (cirrhosis) makes it hard for blood to flow through properly, pressure builds up in the blood vessels. This pushes fluid out into the belly, a condition we call ascites.

question: How can cultural stigma around birth defects affect parents in some communities?

options.A: It forces traditional healers to cure the baby overnight
options.B: It stops the baby from feeling any physical pain
options.C: It can cause feelings of shame, guilt, and isolation
options.D: It guarantees instant government financial aid

explanation: Negative community attitudes and superstitions often leave parents carrying heavy, unfair burdens of self-blame and heartbreak.

question: How many blood vessels are normally inside a healthy human umbilical cord?

options.A: Two arteries and two veins
options.B: Two veins and one artery
options.C: Two arteries and one vein
options.D: One artery and one vein

explanation: Correct! A normal umbilical cord has three vessels: two umbilical arteries carrying waste away from the baby, and one umbilical vein bringing fresh oxygen and nutrients. Easy peasy!

question: What does a nurse suspect when thick blood clots keep blocking a urinary catheter?

options.A: Complete failure of the patient's kidneys to filter blood
options.B: An allergic reaction to the latex material of the drainage bag
options.C: Internal obstruction of the lumen requiring patency check or irrigation
options.D: A normal healing process that requires no nursing intervention

explanation: Clots and debris can clog up the inside of the tube like a blocked drain, meaning you'll need to check if it's patent or flush it.

question: A newborn has a persistent shunt directing blood from the pulmonary artery to the aorta. What structure failed to manage this normal foetal pathway?

options.A: The foramen ovale
options.B: The ductus arteriosus
options.C: The ductus venosus
options.D: The umbilical vein

explanation: The ductus arteriosus is the specific vessel connecting the pulmonary artery to the aorta during foetal life. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T8#GNS121_U6_T8_h4)

question: What is the main goal of post-abortion care (PAC) in the ward?

options.A: To investigate the legal circumstances surrounding the pregnancy
options.B: To conduct routine cervical cancer screening procedures
options.C: To provide permanent family planning counseling for all women
options.D: To treat incomplete or unsafe abortions and manage complications

explanation: PAC is an emergency service to help women safely recover from incomplete or unsafe abortions. You've got this!

question: Which special scan uses a tiny, safe radioactive substance to check for active changes in body tissues?

options.A: Basic fluoroscopy
options.B: Ultrasound
options.C: PET scan
options.D: Standard X-ray

explanation: A PET scan uses a special tracer to light up how tissues and organs are working on a cellular level. Pretty neat technology!

question: Why must nurses monitor clients with neurological problems so closely?

options.A: Hospital insurance policies require hourly doctor visits
options.B: Small changes in condition can rapidly lead to major health crises
options.C: Clients with brain injuries usually refuse all oral medications
options.D: Nervous system tissues heal completely within a few hours

explanation: Because the central nervous system controls vital functions, even tiny changes in behavior or alertness can signal a dangerous decline. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T21#GNS222_U3_T21_h1)

question: Which member of the palliative team usually helps families navigate money troubles and community resources?

options.A: Social worker
options.B: Pharmacist
options.C: Surgeon
options.D: Physical therapist

explanation: You're right! Palliative social workers are lifesavers when it comes to connecting families with financial aid, support groups, and community resources.

question: What is another common name for non-specific body defences?

options.A: Innate immunity
options.B: Active immunity
options.C: Passive immunity
options.D: Adaptive immunity

explanation: Innate immunity refers to the built-in, non-specific defence mechanisms that protect the body from birth. [learn more](GST114_U4_T4#GST114_U4_T4_h1)

question: Why is it important to check expiration dates immediately upon receiving new supplies?

options.A: To calculate the exact financial cost of each individual item
options.B: To determine how many nursing staff members are needed on duty
options.C: To decide which shelf in the storage cupboard looks the cleanest
options.D: To prevent accepting short-dated stock that might expire before use

explanation: Catching expired or near-expiry goods upon delivery allows the facility to return them before accepting responsibility for wasted items. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h6)

question: If the hospital lab is delayed in processing routine blood tests, what will most likely happen?

options.A: The hospital building immediately loses electricity and water
options.B: Patients are discharged earlier to free up hospital beds
options.C: Physician rounds and medication administration are stalled
options.D: Nurses automatically receive extra help from administrative staff

explanation: Because clinical elements are connected, delayed lab results hold up the next steps like doctor rounds and giving treatments. Great clinical awareness!

question: A patient with an injury to their supplementary motor area would have the hardest time doing which of these?

options.A: Playing a practiced song on the piano from memory
options.B: Seeing a bright flashing light across the hospital room
options.C: Reflexively pulling a hand away from a hot stove burner
options.D: Feeling the texture of a piece of smooth velvet fabric

explanation: Playing an instrument takes smoothly linked, sequential movements—which is right up the SMA's alley!

question: What is the main use of a Short-Acting Beta-Agonist (SABA)?

options.A: Suppressing a chronic, non-productive daytime cough
options.B: Lowering high blood pressure in emergency hypertension
options.C: Providing rapid relief during an acute asthma attack
options.D: Controlling daily inflammation over a twelve-month period

explanation: SABAs work in minutes! They are your trusty 'rescue' inhalers used to quickly stop sudden breathlessness during an asthma attack.

question: How is the care for a stable patient with a bruised heart (contusion) different from someone with a bleeding heart wound?

options.A: The blunt injury patient requires immediate open-heart surgery every time.
options.B: The blunt injury patient often receives monitoring and supportive care instead of immediate surgery.
options.C: Medical management is never used for any form of chest trauma.
options.D: Penetrating injuries are always treated with rest and pain medication alone.

explanation: If a patient is stable with a bruised heart, we usually watch them closely in the ICU. But an active stab or gunshot wound? That needs immediate surgery!

question: What is a major advantage of tele-counselling in modern dietary practice?

options.A: Completely replacing the need for any human communication
options.B: Breaking down distance barriers to make regular follow-ups easier
options.C: Guaranteeing that every patient has perfect internet connection
options.D: Requiring all patients to have expensive medical equipment at home

explanation: Tele-counselling allows patients in remote or distant areas to speak with healthcare providers without travelling. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T002#GNS227_U7_T002_h7)

question: What is a likely result when nurses on a ward lack motivation?

options.A: Increased risk of clinical errors and high staff turnover
options.B: Better compliance with mandatory documentation standards
options.C: Decreased utilization of hospital supply inventories
options.D: Faster recovery times for postoperative surgical patients

explanation: When the team is burned out and unmotivated, mistakes happen more easily, and nurses tend to leave. Keeping morale up keeps patients safer!

question: Why might some families prefer that health information be given to an elder rather than the patient?

options.A: The family is trying to hide insurance information from the hospital
options.B: Medical staff prefer speaking to older relatives over younger ones
options.C: The patient legally lacks the ability to understand any medical data
options.D: Cultural norms may dictate shared or family-centered decision-making

explanation: In many cultures, medical decisions are a collective family responsibility rather than an isolated individual choice. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T6#GNS321_U4_T6_h7)

question: Why does a strong primary health care system help major teaching hospitals?

options.A: It ensures that nurses never have to work night shifts again
options.B: It eliminates the need for any laboratory testing supplies
options.C: It allows doctors to retire at an early age
options.D: It prevents tertiary hospitals from becoming overwhelmed with preventable conditions

explanation: Well reasoned! When local clinics handle everyday health issues, big hospitals stay clear and ready for truly complex cases.

question: Which group of psychiatric drugs is most famous for causing rapid weight gain?

options.A: Short-acting sleeping tablets
options.B: Standard over-the-counter vitamins
options.C: Mild herbal anxiety supplements
options.D: Second-generation antipsychotics

explanation: Correct! These medications heavily impact metabolism and appetite control, often leading to rapid weight gain.

question: Which of the following is a primary advantage of the sublingual route?

options.A: Zero risk of side effects
options.B: No need for blood circulation
options.C: Longer duration than injections
options.D: Rapid onset of action

explanation: Direct absorption into blood vessels gives sublingual medicines a very fast therapeutic effect. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T17#GNS125_U3_T17_h4)

question: Which nursing action is most important for preventing infection in a vulval wound after surgery?

options.A: Massaging the labia with scented oils twice a day
options.B: Performing regular perineal hygiene and keeping the area dry
options.C: Encouraging heavy physical exercise to boost circulation
options.D: Applying ice packs directly to the surgical site for 48 hours

explanation: You got it! Keeping the perineal area clean and dry stops bacteria from nearby pathways from infecting the fresh surgical wound.

question: What makes epilepsy different from having just one isolated seizure?

options.A: Epilepsy involves recurrent, unprovoked seizures over time
options.B: Epilepsy can only be diagnosed using a blood test
options.C: Epilepsy only occurs in children under the age of five
options.D: Single seizures are always fatal while epilepsy is mild

explanation: Anyone can have a one-off seizure due to a temporary trigger like a very high fever. Epilepsy is diagnosed when someone has repeated seizures that happen without a clear, immediate trigger.

question: How does government-funded agricultural research benefit the general public?

options.A: By ensuring that farming requires zero human labor input
options.B: By developing pest-resistant crops that secure the food supply
options.C: By removing all regulations on chemical pesticide usage
options.D: By discovering new ways to make processed foods last indefinitely

explanation: Research creates stronger, higher-yield crops that protect against harvest failures and maintain stable food availability. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h3)

question: When can palliative care be introduced during the course of a serious illness?

options.A: At any stage alongside life-prolonging treatments
options.B: Exclusively after all curative options have failed
options.C: Only when the patient is discharged back home
options.D: Only during the final twenty-four hours of life

explanation: Palliative care is not just for end-of-life; it can and should be integrated early alongside disease-modifying or curative treatments. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h1)

question: Why do adult males typically have a higher resting metabolic rate than females of the same size?

options.A: Their digestive tract is physically longer
options.B: Their baseline body temperature is higher
options.C: Their brains require more glucose hourly
options.D: They generally have a higher percentage of lean muscle mass

explanation: Great job thinking through this! Men naturally tend to have more muscle mass than women, and since muscle burns more calories at rest, their baseline calorie need is higher.

question: When we talk about 'sex' in human health, what are we mainly referring to?

options.A: Physical and physiological traits
options.B: Cultural roles assigned at birth
options.C: Socially constructed behaviors
options.D: Personal expressions of identity

explanation: You've got this! 'Sex' refers to our biological makeup—like chromosomes, hormones, and anatomy—which is different from the social roles we play.

question: Why are clients told to avoid caffeine before doing a cardiac stress test?

options.A: Caffeine lowers blood pressure to dangerous levels
options.B: Caffeine makes the ECG machine run out of paper faster
options.C: Caffeine can artificially speed up the heart rate and interfere with test findings
options.D: Caffeine causes severe stomach cramps during exercise

explanation: That's right! Stimulants like coffee or tea affect heart rhythm, making it tough to measure how the heart truly responds to exercise.

question: What is the most common hormonal condition behind oligomenorrhoea in young women?

options.A: Type 1 diabetes mellitus
options.B: Addison's disease
options.C: Cushing's disease
options.D: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome

explanation: You'll see this condition a lot in clinical practice! Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) is the leading hormonal cause of irregular, spaced-out periods.

question: How does family planning directly promote gender equality?

options.A: By making biological differences between men and women disappear
options.B: By giving women control over their reproductive lives so they can pursue education and work
options.C: By ensuring that only women make decisions regarding community finances
options.D: By legally prohibiting men from participating in healthcare discussions

explanation: Fertility control frees women from the cycle of constant childrearing, enabling them to pursue personal and professional goals on equal footing. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T002#GNS226_U6_T002_h4)

question: What skin pigment protects cells from ultraviolet light damage?

options.A: Hemoglobin
options.B: Keratin
options.C: Melanin
options.D: Carotene

explanation: Melanin is produced by melanocytes to absorb harmful ultraviolet radiation from the sun. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T5#GNS211_U2_T5_h2)

question: What happens if you manage to disrupt just one single link in the chain of infection?

options.A: The pathogen automatically changes into a harmless virus
options.B: The susceptible host becomes permanently immune
options.C: The infection process is completely stopped
options.D: The reservoir doubles its reproductive rate

explanation: Brilliant! The chain needs every single link to stay connected. Break just one, and the disease is stopped in its tracks.

question: What structural feature keeps the trachea open and stops it from collapsing?

options.A: Smooth muscle sheets inside the lumen
options.B: Horseshoe-shaped cartilage rings
options.C: Dense networks of elastic ligaments
options.D: Thick layers of stratified epithelium

explanation: Think of those horseshoe-shaped cartilage rings as sturdy scaffolding that keeps the windpipe open against everyday neck pressures. Simple and brilliant!

question: What does a bulging anterior fontanelle usually mean in a newborn?

options.A: Normal developmental closure
options.B: Severe systemic dehydration
options.C: Premature fusion of the skull
options.D: Increased intracranial pressure

explanation: Spot on! Extra pressure inside the head pushes the soft membrane outward, causing that tight, bulging feel.

question: Which pillar of nursing informatics provides the hardware, software, and network tools?

options.A: Nursing science
options.B: Information science
options.C: Computer science
options.D: Biological science

explanation: Computer science deals with the physical technology, software, and systems used to process and store digital information. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T1#GNS113_U1_T1_h3)

question: Which nutrient is most often missing in unfortified gluten-free grain alternatives?

options.A: Sodium
options.B: Potassium
options.C: B vitamins
options.D: Vitamin C

explanation: Standard wheat products are usually fortified with B vitamins like folate, which alternative flours often lack unless added back.

question: What is the primary benefit of connecting a newly diagnosed patient to a peer support group?

options.A: It normalizes their experience and shows them that people can live long, healthy lives with HIV
options.B: It cures the viral infection within a few weeks of consistent meetings
options.C: It provides them with free housing and government food supplies
options.D: It legally waives their responsibility to ever inform their sexual partners

explanation: Peer groups reduce feelings of isolation by introducing patients to others who are thriving despite their diagnosis. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T8#GNS216_U6_T8_h7)

question: Why are worm infections so common in places with poor sanitation?

options.A: Parasitic eggs are easily spread through contaminated soil and water
options.B: Lack of refrigeration causes food to turn directly into parasites
options.C: Humid air causes human skin to produce worm larvae
options.D: Poor lighting weakens the human immune system against worms

explanation: Spot on! Worm eggs often pass through feces into soil and water supplies, which easily infect new people if hygiene is lacking.

question: Why do patients with chronic glomerulonephritis sometimes notice foamy urine?

options.A: High amounts of sugar
options.B: Too many white blood cells
options.C: Presence of excess protein
options.D: Excessive water intake

explanation: You've got this! When damaged glomeruli let large protein molecules slip through into the urine, it creates bubbles, giving the urine a noticeable foamy look.

question: Which pillar of safe motherhood focuses on checking on the mother and baby right after childbirth?

options.A: Family planning
options.B: Obstetric care
options.C: Antenatal care
options.D: Postnatal care

explanation: Well done! Postnatal care happens after delivery to make sure both mother and baby are recovering smoothly.

question: A community health nurse organizes a blood pressure screening exercise at the local market. What level of prevention is this?

options.A: Primary prevention
options.B: Primordial prevention
options.C: Tertiary prevention
options.D: Secondary prevention

explanation: Screenings are designed for early detection of health problems so that intervention can start before complications develop. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h4)

question: What is the main characteristic of a nursing team in the performing stage?

options.A: They are preparing to permanently disband the unit
options.B: They constantly argue about who should do shift handovers
options.C: They are just getting to know each other and remain very polite
options.D: They work together smoothly to achieve high-quality care

explanation: In the performing stage, the team operates with high synergy, trust, and efficiency. [learn more](GST321_U7_T1#GST321_U7_T1_h3)

question: How does nursing in the community differ from working in a big hospital ward?

options.A: Home nurses rely heavily on resourcefulness and critical thinking in the community.
options.B: Home nurses have direct access to immediate physician support at all times.
options.C: Hospital nurses perform fewer physical assessments than community nurses.
options.D: Hospital nurses manage fewer complex chronic conditions than home nurses.

explanation: You got it! Without hospital equipment and doctors right next door, home care nurses have to trust their training, think on their feet, and solve problems creatively.

question: Why is there fluid between the thin membranes that wrap around our organs?

options.A: To transmit nerve signals to the brain
options.B: To digest food particles in the stomach
options.C: To carry oxygen through the bloodstream
options.D: To reduce friction during organ movement

explanation: Imagine two sliding doors with oil between them. This fluid lubricates the membranes so your heart and lungs can glide smoothly without rubbing raw!

question: In sickle cell disease, what causes red blood cells to bend into a crescent or 'sickle' shape?

options.A: Abnormal hemoglobin molecules
options.B: Low white blood cell counts
options.C: Excess dietary iron intake
options.D: Rapid platelet activation

explanation: Spot on! The hemoglobin inside the red blood cells has a slight structural change. When oxygen levels drop, these altered molecules stick together and pull the cell into that famous sickle shape.

question: When is the right time to start transmission-based precautions for a patient?

options.A: At the first sign of symptoms or upon suspicion of infection
options.B: After public health officers visit the ward
options.C: When the patient requests a private hospital room
options.D: Only after laboratory confirmation is fully finalized
